data.narrative:
Project Omega, a Seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Stafford Sheehan, has raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader nuclear energy comp universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities including Nano Nuclear Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

Only one valuation method proved applicable. The Stage-Progression approach, anchored to the $12M raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of the Seed-to-next-stage transition in frontier technology. This yields an implied valuation of $30M. A Peer-Median approach was not viable; while 6 same-sector peers exist, the narrow filters for stage alignment and comparable valuation tier produced insufficient datapoints (fewer than 3 required), and a broader cross-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise.

The triangulated range supported by this analysis is $26M (low) to $34M (high), with a median of $30M. This narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodology rather than convergence across multiple methods. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for the nuclear subsector specifically, and the absence of directly comparable private company valuations at identical stage and scale. Future rounds with market-tested pricing or expanded peer data would sharpen this estimate.
